Subject: Post-demo: Long-history summarization fidelity & model recommendations

Hi Rachel / Dan,

Thanks again for the demo today — appreciate the walkthrough of CareSight's long patient visit histories and the concrete failure cases you showed (duplicated notes, inline doctor commentary, and encounter-level metadata you want preserved). Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

What we heard
- Typical doc length: 12–20 encounters (~18k tokens raw) with important context scattered across the middle.
- Primary goal: faithful chronological summarization (visit-level bullets) + extract key meds/changes.
- Constraints: 200ms P95 token latency target for interactive UI; pilot budget ~50k tokens/day.

Immediate risks we flagged
- Truncation can drop mid-encounter details; naive windowing hurts fidelity.
- Aggressive summarization models may hallucinate dates/meds if prompts aren't anchored.

Recommended short plan
1) Run a small long-context eval (2 weeks) using 100 representative patient histories. We will run: two LLM variants (open large + quantized medium) and one Redwood-optimized variant with prefix caching.
2) Benchmarks we deliver: summarization ROUGE/ROUGE-L, factuality checks (medication extraction precision/recall), and token latency/cost breakdown.
3) Prompt set: we shared a first-pass prompt set attached (caresight_prompt_set_v1.jsonl) — please flag obvious edge cases.
4) Decision criteria: vendor/model that keeps meds precision >= 95% while meeting 200ms P95 or cost < $0.0008/token on pilot traffic.

Attachments: caresight_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (prompt variants + anchoring examples)

Next actions
- From you: confirm 100-record sample and redacted dataset access timeline (we discussed SFTP/Drive).
- From us: we’ll run a quick smoke benchmark and share SUMMARY_BENCHMARKS.csv + a short playbook (redwood_long_context_playbook.pdf) by end of week.

If it helps, we can scope a short call on Wed to lock the sample and SLAs — 30 minutes should do it.

Cheers,
Kimberly Park

Rachel — great, thanks for the quick turnaround. Answers below and an alternate plan for the single-pass vs chunk+merge- We’ll include three eval arms:
   a) Single-pass large model (open checkpoint, full sequence where possible via Redwood streaming + KV caching).
   b) Chunk+merge (4k windows summarised then merged with a second-pass model).
   c) Quantized low-cost variant with prefix caching and explicit anchoring prompts (best-effort chronology).
We’ll measure chronology preservation with an event-ordering metric and compare hallucination rates.

2) Factuality checks- Two-stage: automated extraction (rule-based NER + med normalization) to produce candidate med lists, followed by sampled human adjudication (10% sample) to estimate precision/recall. We’ll include disagreement rates in the benchmark CSV.

Benchmarks & primer links
- Summary benchmarks: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/long-context/v2
- Pilot playbook (attached): redwood_long_context_playbook.pdf

Prompting notes (high level)
- Anchor prompts around encounter headers (date/time, provider) and require explicit "source token" outputs (e.g., <SRC:encounter-5>) for any extracted med/date to reduce free-form hallucination.
- We included prompt variants in caresight_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (short/long/in-context examples). Use the "anchored_extraction" profile to start.

Attachments: SUMMARY_BENCHMARKS.csv (sample results from a 20-record smoke run — highlights: single-pass large kept meds precision 97% but P95 latency was 420ms; chunk+merge reduced P95 to 180ms with meds precision 93%)

Proposed pilot timeline
- Thu (Nov 5): CareSight sends 100 redacted records.
- Fri (Nov 6): We run smoke benchmarks and share full CSV + playbook.
- Mon (Nov 9): Joint review call to pick the model variant for a 2-week pilot.

Can we lock Wed 10am PT for the ops call and Thu delivery for the sample? If so, I’ll send a calendar invite and a short MxP (mutual action plan) doc.

Thanks — kim
